Not-worth-doing, per the design's own escape hatch. No Docker/CI infra exists in this repo (confirmed: no Dockerfile, no .github/workflows - CI was explicitly out of scope at epic creation) to pin a reproducible rendering environment, and this exact worktree is WSL2/Linux/x64. toHaveScreenshot baselines generated here would only match runs on the same OS/Chromium build; any contributor on macOS or Windows running npm run test:e2e would get spurious pixel diffs on every unrelated content edit. The skill's own audience is explicitly non-technical site owners who edit content/images regularly, not developers who would know to regenerate baselines via --update-snapshots or a container - that is precisely the abandonment failure mode the design called out. The .5 smoke suite already gives real automated coverage (exact heading text, nav, footer, broken images, uncaught page errors) without this fragility, so relying on it instead is a clean substitute rather than a gap.
